title: A redesigned practice dashboard with patient lists and completed kidney testing in type 2 diabetes: a cohort study across a staggered rollout
abstract: Objective: to estimate whether a redesigned dashboard with peer comparison, a target and a patient list increases completed kidney testing in type 2 diabetes. Design: cohort of about 4,900 patients due for testing in 31 practices, comparing 16 practices that received the dashboard in March 2026 with 15 that received it in September 2026. Outcome: both tests resulted within the window. Results and conclusions will follow the analysis.
introduction: Audit and feedback produces small average improvements, and patient-level lists may be the feature that turns feedback into action. Ordered tests overstate completion and feedback can cause duplicate testing, so both are measured.
methods: Pseudonymised extracts and usage logs; mixed-effects logistic regression with practice random intercept and baseline adjustment; pre-rollout trends compared between waves; duplicate testing as a balancing measure.
results: No data have been analysed yet. The report will present pre-rollout trends, completion by wave, the adjusted risk difference, list use and duplicate testing.
discussion: The discussion will compare the estimate with the retrieved feedback literature and state whether the patient list should be kept, changed or dropped. One cited comparison of patient lists was later found to carry an identifier for a different work and must be re-checked before the report cites it.
limitations: Non-random timing; imprecision; incomplete hospital linkage.
conclusion: To be written after analysis; it will not cite unchecked leads.
summary: STROBE-structured draft with results left empty.
